newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's c.bank trims rates, sees further cuts.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's c.bank trims rates, sees further cuts.

text.p: Croatia's central bank said it had cut the mandatory reserve requirement for banks and savings banks by one percentage point to 33.85 percent for June, in line with indicators pointing to an overall reduction in interest rates.
In a statement released after Wednesday's monthly board meeting the bank said it would also cut the rate on mandatory reserve deposits to 4.5 from 5.5 percent.

"The liquidity of commercial banks during the last months was subject to changes. This was reflected in money market rates and in the activity of the central bank in the foreign exchange market," the bank said.
"But there were no major disturbances so data for May are expected to show a further reduction of commercial banks' interest rates," it said.
Croatia's macroeconomic stability was stable in May, with the exchange rate of the domestic currency kuna remaining stable against the German mark.
The retail price index grew 0.4 percent from April while it remained stable at 3.6 percent year-on-year.
The number of unemployed fell in April after several months of continued growth.

Real wages in the first four months of the year were on average 12.7 percent higher than in the same period last year, but were estimated not to be in "significant disproportion" with productivity trends and were therefore non-inflationary.
The central bank noted what it described as a "positive trend of growth" in production, trade, construction and tourism -- the last being a strategic base for the development of Croatia's economy.

The rise in exports from January to May "has been visible" compared to the same period in 1996, but was overshadowed by an even stronger rise in imports, the statement said. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-457075
